thread:
ben-support: Heads up — Acme reporting a big spike in 503s for hosted inference starting ~11:02. CS ticket CS-1234. They pasted an error: "upstream inference worker exited unexpectedly" and request IDs.

ben-support: sample error they sent:
```
2025-10-21T11:03:12Z ERROR upstream: worker pid=12345 exit signal=SIGABRT code=0x1 req_id=acme-req-7f9a
2025-10-21T11:03:12Z WARN nvml: GPU 0 OOM while allocating 122MB
```

alice-eng: thx. which model/version + region? any auth failures mentioned or just 503s?

ben-support: model: redwood/mammoth-13b-quant-v2, region: us-west-2, customer says calls come back 503 with no body sometimes. No auth errors seen.

maria-oncall: I can see correlated worker restarts in the infra logs in us-west-2 around 11:02-11:06. Process exit looks like SIGABRT w/ CUDA OOM in dmesg.

raj-sre: attaching kernel segfault? paste from host tail:
```
[ 11:03:11 ] infer-runner[12345]: runtime error: cuda runtime error (2): out of memory
[ 11:03:11 ] infer-runner[12345]: aborting: unhandled exception
```

alice-eng: Was there a deploy or model swap just before 11:02? deploy-bot, any recent canary?

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: model-swap redwood/mammoth-13b-quant-v2 @ 2025-10-21T10:58:43 by alice-eng (traffic 20% -> 100% at 11:00:05)

raj-sre: that timing lines up. quant-v2 swap -> sudden mem pattern change -> OOMs. Might be kvcache prefetch pattern + increased batch sizes.

ops-bot: routing rule: fallback to mammoth-13b-quant-v1 available in pool us-west-2

alice-eng: immediate triage steps: 1) rollback model to quant-v1 2) reduce batch size / disable prefetch 3) collect core + nvml logs for one crashed worker 4) try local repro with stress script.

ben-support: acme is in a call, they want a mitigation now. Can you roll back?

alice-eng: initiating rollback now. deploy-bot: rollback-start redwood/mammoth-13b-quant-v1 -> 100% @ 11:07:12

maria-oncall: rolling traffic to fallback. I'll watch for residual 503s.

raj-sre: while rollback proceeds, please grab one of the crashed container logs and a backtrace. Use `kubectl -n hosted logs <pod> --previous` and `gdb --batch --ex "bt full" --pid <pid>` if core present. Also collect `/var/log/nvml.log` and `dmesg`.

ben-support: asked CS to collect pod name and upload logs to the ticket. They sent `hosted-infer-az1-pod-5f8c9` and recent `kubectl logs --previous` output.

alice-eng: quick glance at their `--previous` logs shows: 
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
nvml: GPU 0 failed allocation at 0x7f9b4000 size=134217728
```

raj-sre: that `bad_alloc` + nvml OOM suggests quant runtime changed memory layout; we could be hitting a fragmentation edge on bigger batch sizes. Action: pin the model, and create canary with batch-limit=1 and prefetch=off for quant-v2.

alice-eng: Created task ENG-2311 to reproduce with same model and an internal script: `scripts/repro/high_qps_batch.sh --model redwood/mammoth-13b-quant-v2 --batch 8 --context 2048`. Sharing link to runbook snippet.

maria-oncall: rollback completed @ 11:07:40. 503 rate dropped to baseline in ~2 min. CS confirms partial recovery but still seeing timeouts for long streaming calls.

ben-support: customer acknowledged rollback helped, they want root cause + ETA for a fix. CS asked about billing credits.

raj-sre: triage notes: reproducible OOM when quant-v2 is under sustained batched streaming with prefetch=on. Hypothesis: new quant kernel uses larger temporary workspace per token causing memory ballooning during KV prefetch. Need heap/core analysis + run under profiler.

alice-eng: next steps I assigned: 1) reproduce in staging with same hardware config (ENG-2311) 2) add guardrails: enforce batch limits and disable prefetch for canary 3) prepare hotfix build with safer allocator / smaller workspace 4) coordinate CS message and potential credit.

maria-oncall: collecting core files + nvml-smi snapshots, uploading to s3://redwood-debug/acme-1765559998/. Link: https://s3.redwood/acme-1765559998/core-archive.zip

ben-support: CS notified customer that we rolled back and are investigating. They asked for ETA; told them ~24-48h for root-cause + patch.

raj-sre: FYI we also saw a pattern of `prefetch()` allocating a contiguous buffer ~120MB per active request; with concurrency >3 we exceed GPU memory after workspace and KV. We'll add throttles at the routing layer to cap concurrency per worker until fix is out.

alice-eng: enabling routing throttle now: ops-bot apply-config throttle.concurrency.per_worker=3 for redwood/mammoth-13b-quant-v2 (canary).

ops-bot: config-apply: throttle.concurrency.per_worker=3 applied to canary pool @ 11:32:15

raj-sre: long-term: adjust quant kernel workspace and add allocator fallback to spill to host if transient. Also add automated perf test for prefetch+batch combos.

maria-oncall: monitoring shows 503s at baseline post-rollback. Logging remaining as INFO. Marking incident as mitigated.

ben-support: closing loop with CS, will escalate billing credits separately. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

alice-eng: follow-ups: ENG-2311 (repro), ENG-2312 (hotfix allocator), SRE-447 (routing throttle guard). I'll post summaries in the incident doc.

raj-sre: arch note: avoid sudden 100% traffic switches for quant builds until perf validation completes. Recommend staged ramp with autosafety gates.

ben-support: noted. If anyone needs further details from the customer CS-1234 will keep logs attached.
